newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak says Arab summit now would be premature.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak says Arab summit now would be premature.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Monday that an Arab summit now would be premature and Israeli-Palestinian differences were not a sufficient reason for holding one.
"I believe that it is not yet the time for an Arab summit now," he told reporters during a tour of Sadat City, an industrial satellite city northwest of Cairo.
"There have to be reasons which allow for that. The positon of the last Arab summit was that peace is a strategic option so let's wait and see what happens," he added.
The last summit, and the first since 1990, took place in Cairo in June, shortly after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office at the head of a rightwing government.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has been campaigning for another summit by the end of the year. He has said the summit should include Iraq, which was not invited to Cairo in June.

But Mubarak said: "Holding an Arab summit must have a strong reason. If there is still a dispute between the Palestinians and the Israelis over implementation (of peace agreements), this does not call for holding an Arab summit at all."
On Sunday Mubarak's foreign minister, Amr Moussa, was also cool to the idea of an early Arab summit.

"Holding an Arab summit requires certain measures and dynamics and we are still following up implementation of the decisions of the last summit. The question of holding a summit at the present time depends on what circumstances dictate and what Arab action requires," Moussa said.
